proxy.title: Use {{name}} as a proxy
proxy.lede: Send another device's traffic through {{name}}, so it leaves from {{name}}'s address. Put this address in any browser, app or script.
proxy.secret: Works like a password: anyone with it can use {{name}}'s proxy.
proxy.what: It is an HTTP proxy reached over an encrypted connection. Secure sites pass through it encrypted end to end, and plain web pages are forwarded. Traffic leaves from {{name}}'s own IP address, unless you set another exit below.
proxy.limits: Without another exit, it reaches public IPv4 addresses only. Private and local addresses are refused. If you set another exit, that exit decides which sites work, and IPv6 addresses are still refused.
proxy.noAddress: The address shows once the computer's server is known.
proxy.stopped: {{name}} is stopped. The proxy answers once it runs again.
proxy.curl.help: One request through the proxy. The second line asks a site which address it saw, so you can check the route.
proxy.curl.label: curl through the proxy
proxy.unix.help: In a terminal, these lines send curl, git, pip and most other tools through the proxy until you close that terminal.
proxy.unix.label: Shell settings
proxy.windows.help: In PowerShell, for that window only. Tools that read these settings, such as curl and git, then go through the proxy.
proxy.windows.label: PowerShell settings
proxy.node.help: Node's own fetch uses the proxy once proxy support is on: no package, no code change. Set the address, then start your app with the flag or variable.
proxy.node.label: Node.js through the proxy
proxy.system.help: Only need a browser? The separate Chrome window is simpler. Otherwise the system setting needs this file at a web address: Chrome won't read file:///.
proxy.system.host.help: An https:// address with a trusted certificate and no sign-in prompt (the setting can't sign in). Keep it private: the file holds the proxy address.
proxy.system.enter.help: As the automatic proxy configuration (setup script).
proxy.system.mac.path: System Settings, Network, your network, Details, Proxies, Automatic proxy configuration.
proxy.system.win.path: Settings, Network & internet, Proxy, Use setup script.
proxy.system.fails: If it can't load the file
proxy.system.fails.help: Browsing goes out directly from your own address, without warning.
proxy.system.label: proxy.pac for the system setting
proxy.check: To check a setup, open https://ip.hoody.com through it. It shows the address sites see: {{name}}'s own address, or its exit's if you set one.
proxy.onlyMe.docs: Limit it to your IP in access rules
proxy.exit.title: Other ways to change the exit
proxy.exit.lede: Sites see {{name}}'s address by default. There are three ways to change that. The first is what Use another exit… sets on the Network tab.
proxy.exit.up.title: Through a proxy you already have
proxy.exit.up.body: Set it as {{name}}'s exit (socks5h, socks5, http or https). While it can't be used, requests are refused, never sent from {{name}}'s own address.
proxy.exit.up.label: Upstream proxy
proxy.exit.off.label: Back to its own address
proxy.exit.up.set: Use a proxy (put its address in place of PROXY_HOST:1080)
proxy.exit.local.title: From your own machine
proxy.exit.local.body: Run it signed in to the hoody command-line tool. Until Ctrl+C, requests leave from your machine: anyone with the proxy address uses your connection.
proxy.exit.local.label: Exit from this machine
proxy.exit.local.docs: Exit from your own machine in the docs
proxy.exit.vpn.title: With a VPN inside {{name}}
proxy.exit.vpn.body: Add an SSH key first (your way back in). Run your VPN's WireGuard file with wg-quick, not its app: its kill switch cuts {{name}} off, web terminal too.
proxy.exit.vpn.docs: VPN inside a computer in the docs
proxy.uses: Use it as a jump host, to reach sites from {{name}}'s location, or like a VPN so your own network can't see what you browse.
proxy.browser.shared: Don't set this up on a shared or public computer: anyone who can see the address can use {{name}}'s proxy.
proxy.ff.1: Save the proxy file to your computer.
proxy.ff.4: Type where you saved the file, starting with file:///.
proxy.ce.why: Chrome and Edge use the system proxy settings, whose manual fields fail here. Open a separate window: its empty profile leaves your browsing alone.
proxy.ce.win.1: Press the Windows key and R together.
proxy.ce.win.2: Paste the line for your browser and press Enter.
proxy.ce.mac.2: Paste the line for your browser and press Return.
proxy.ce.3: A window opens. Use only it; close it to stop.
proxy.safari.help: Safari uses the Mac's proxy settings. The manual proxy fields there don't work with this proxy: they connect to it without encryption, which it refuses. Use Firefox or a Chrome or Edge window instead.
proxy.phone.help: A phone's Wi-Fi proxy setting doesn't work with this proxy yet: it connects without encryption, which the proxy refuses. Use it from a computer, or from an app that takes an HTTPS proxy (the values at the top).
proxy.values.title: The values, one by one
proxy.values.help: For an app or extension that asks for a proxy type, server and port, use the values at the top. Choose the HTTPS type: an HTTP type won't connect.
proxy.values.login: None. Leave user name and password empty: the address itself is the key.
proxy.how.sub: Send traffic through {{name}} from a browser, an app or a script.
proxy.ff.2.note: Then press Settings… next to Network Settings.
proxy.ff.4.note: Change YOU to your user name, or the folder if you saved it somewhere else.
proxy.ff.5.note: Only Firefox uses the proxy; to stop, choose No proxy there again.
proxy.values.reach: Public IPv4 addresses only, unless you set another exit
proxy.v.label: Proxy address
proxy.v.sentence: Traffic sent here leaves from {{name}}'s address, unless you set another exit.
proxy.set.chrome: Open a Chrome or Edge window
proxy.good.title: Good to know
